verdict.rationale: Lovable's docs say you can export and sync a project to GitHub or GitLab, or download the codebase, so you can "deploy outside Lovable". That makes self-hosting a documented, product-supported path. However, the evidence gives no deployment guide for any external host or own infrastructure. It also does not address how the built-in Lovable Cloud backend (database, auth, functions) would move off-platform. Missing for 10: documented steps for deploying to external hosts or self-managed infrastructure, portability of the Cloud/Supabase backend outside Lovable, and independent or hands-on confirmation of an external deploy.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy the generated app to an external host or my own infrastructure

citations.quote: you can export and sync your project to GitHub: back up your code, review changes in pull requests, work locally in your IDE, test features on branches, and deploy outside Lovable
If you only need a copy of your code, you can download your code directly from Lovable: use the Download codebase section in Project settings → Git
Git sync connects a Lovable project to a repository you own on GitHub or GitLab, and keeps the two in sync automatically
